question: Ozanne-Rivierre's Table 3.3.4 (Haudricourt & Ozanne-Rivierre 1982: 54-55) gives POc > 'langues de Hienghène' for all four languages at once, naming a language only where they differ. How is it entered?
chosen_reading: One row per language (Pije, Fwâi, Nemi, Jawe), composed POc > PNC > language with the printed cell in as_printed; a cell without a language label applies to all four, except that Fwâi gets no row whose reflex is an oral stop or strong continuant other than word-finally, since these occur in Fwâi only in loans (p. 18) and Fwâi turns intervocalic stops into continuants or zero (§1.6, p. 14). Her notation -x (now final) and -x- (still intervocalic) for a medial POc consonant becomes the environments 'V_V, now word-final' and 'V_V'; several reflexes in one position are entered with conditioning unknown (the conditions are discussed in §3.3, not tabulated). Her POc letters are mapped to Ross's (*d = r, *nd = dr, *nt = d, *mp = b, *ŋp = bʷ, *ŋm = mʷ, *ŋk = ɡ). POc *l and *ñ, merged with *n in PNC, keep their own rows with conditioning 'lexical'. *R > ∅ in all positions is not entered (PNC has already lost *R), nor are the vowels of Table 3.3.4 B (*a > a, e; *e > e, Pije also a; *i > i; *o > e, (o); *u > u, i; *ai > e; *au > o; p. 55), since PNC has no vowels in the database (Ozanne-Rivierre 1992 does not discuss them). The palatal rows ((*s-), (*-s-) and *-j-, (*ns-), (*-ns-)) are not entered: by n. 57 her (*s) is Grace's *ns and her (*ns) Grace's *s, and her *-j- (Ross's *c) is grouped with (*-s-), which does not fit Ozanne-Rivierre's (1992) PNC merger of *c with *s.
alternatives: Enter the palatal rows after deciding which Ross phonemes (*s, *j, *c) her (*s), (*ns) and *j are; add Hienghène nodes; read §3.3 to give each alternative its condition.
